title: Yash's 'Toxic' Crosses Rs 200 Crore in India Net Collections by Day 5
excerpt: The gangster actioner directed by Geetu Mohandas has surpassed Rs 255 crore worldwide and continues its strong first-weekend run.
body:
• 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' crossed Rs 204 crore in India net collections on Day 5, adding an estimated Rs 13.13 crore from 11,373 shows.
  • The film's worldwide gross has surpassed Rs 255 crore, with overseas markets contributing steadily each day.
  • Hindi remains the dominant language, contributing Rs 8.23 crore on Day 5, followed by Kannada at Rs 3.97 crore.
  • The film opened to Rs 101.10 crore on Day 1 — one of the biggest openings for a Kannada-origin film in Indian cinema.

Yash's much-anticipated gangster drama 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' has crossed the Rs 200 crore milestone in India net collections on its fifth day of release, according to tracking data from Sacnilk. The film, directed by Geetu Mohandas and co-written by Yash and Mohandas, earned an estimated Rs 13.13 crore net on Day 5 from 11,373 shows, bringing its cumulative India net total to Rs 204.23 crore.

A Blockbuster Opening Weekend

Released on August 26, 'Toxic' opened to a massive Rs 101.10 crore net in India from 24,579 shows — a landmark debut for a Kannada-origin star's pan-India release. The film maintained strong momentum through its first weekend: Day 2 brought in Rs 37.65 crore from 22,629 shows, Day 3 added Rs 27.20 crore, and Day 4 contributed Rs 25.15 crore from 17,612 shows.

While daily collections have followed the expected post-opening decline, the film's India gross climbed to Rs 243.74 crore by Day 5. Worldwide gross collections crossed Rs 255.50 crore by Day 4, with overseas markets adding Rs 4 crore that day.

Language-Wise Breakdown

Hindi prints drove the largest share of Day 5 revenue at Rs 8.23 crore, followed by Kannada at Rs 3.97 crore. Telugu and Tamil contributed Rs 61 lakh and Rs 32 lakh respectively, according to Sacnilk's live tracking. The Hindi-language performance underscores Yash's cross-regional appeal following the 'KGF' franchise.

The Film's Premise

'Toxic' follows the rise of Raya, a crime lord in Goa during Portuguese rule, and the eventual conflict between Raya and his son Ticket — with Yash portraying both characters. The film stars Nayanthara, Kiara Advani, Huma Qureshi, Rukmini Vasanth, and Tara Sutaria in key roles.

What's Next at the Box Office

The critical test for 'Toxic' begins Monday, when weekday collections will determine whether the film can sustain its pace toward the Rs 300 crore India net mark. First-weekend holds have been solid, but the drop from Day 1's Rs 101 crore to Day 5's Rs 13 crore — a roughly 87% decline — is steeper than what 'KGF: Chapter 2' experienced in 2022. Trade analysts will watch closely whether the film can maintain Rs 8-10 crore daily through the first week.

For the Indian diaspora, 'Toxic' marks another milestone in Kannada cinema's expanding global footprint, following the 'KGF' franchise's success in international markets.
